CHALLENGER POSE: reuse the result-stage node-offset machinery (static animation + captureNodePose + poseNode after the mixer). Must read 'confident challenger, bring it on', playful, and must NOT look like the result stage 'celebrate' (arms straight up sideways + hopping) or 'despair' (kneel + fists at ceiling). Direction: planted wide stance (legs splayed slightly on z), torso leaning forward toward camera, head slightly down/forward, both fists thrown up in FRONT (rotate arms on x toward forward-up, elbows implied, not straight sideways), two sharp fist pumps in the first ~0.8 s (fast out, eased back), then held. Optional tiny stomp (0.05-0.08 y dip) on the first pump. Restore rest pose cleanly when returning/at exit/at enter so the rival's later walking/idle animation is not left offset.

CAMERA: a new CHALLENGE_CLOSEUP_CAMERA constant near ENTRANCE_CAMERA. Starting value to tune by render: position ~[-1.35, 1.95, 5.2], lookAt ~[-2.1, 1.3, 2.4] (rival at x -2.1, z 2.4, scale 0.78). The rival must be clearly framed, head and raised fists in frame, at 1366x768 and 412x915 (portrait may pull back along the view line, as fitStageCamera does). Noticeable but not nauseating: no shake, no FOV tricks.

JINGLE: replace the single 'restaurant-rival-sting' with a note sequence played through the existing code-generated audio.playSfx (one oscillator per call; each call needs a unique name or options object; type/frequency/endFrequency/duration/gain). Structure: low cautious warning notes (e.g. two short 'square' or 'triangle' notes around 196-233 Hz), a quick rising run through the walk, then a strong BA-BAM (two punchy chords/stacked notes ~0.12 s apart, louder) fired by the 'reveal' event, not by a fixed time, so it lands on the punch-in. Whole thing ~1.0-1.3 s because the walk is ~1.05 s; alert/exciting, not scary: major or suspended intervals, no minor-second drones. Drive it from the intro clock the way updateResultSting does.

TYPEWRITER: new pure module src/minigames/restaurant/typewriter.js. parseFurigana(source) -> units: each plain character (including kana, punctuation and full-width marks) is one unit; '\n' is kept as a zero-cost line-break unit; each '{kanji|reading}' is ONE ruby unit with cost = base length (勝負 costs 2). createTypewriter({ units, charsPerSecond = 30 }) with advance(dt), revealAll(), revealedCost, totalCost, visibleUnitCount, complete. The scene renders the FULL structure once (each unit a span, ruby units as <ruby>base<rt>reading</rt></ruby> inside their span) and hides unrevealed units with visibility:hidden, so centred lines never reflow while typing and <ruby>/<rt> are never sliced. Keep appendFurigana for the reply buttons (or reimplement it on top of parseFurigana; either way reply rendering must not change). Give the line element an aria-label with the plain sentence.

SPACE / INPUT: while typing, a window capture-phase keydown for Space (and Enter) reveals the rest and is fully consumed (preventDefault + stopImmediatePropagation, repeats too); it must not reach input.js interact, speech Talk (speech target is already cleared during the intro; keep it so), world actions, or a reply. A click/tap on the panel while typing also reveals all (touch users need a skip). A Space/Enter press that skipped the typewriter must not select a reply: do not focus the first reply until that key's keyup has been seen (swallow the keyup and any repeats too), and ignore repeat keydowns for reply activation. After that a fresh press works as today (focused button, arrows move focus, click works). Natural completion replaces the old RIVAL_CHALLENGE_CHOICE_DELAY_SECONDS guard; keep choose() rejecting until choices are visible.
REPLIES appear together: remove the nth-child animation-delay stagger; one shared short appear animation is fine.
PANEL: remove the .restaurant-ui__challenge-name badge (markup, CSS, the textContent assignment). The floating 3D WAITER label is the only name.
